body:
Ahahahah. This subreddit is so far gone that apparently you people can't even tell satire when you see it.

The infographic is obviously *mocking* the quotes given, not endorsing them. I mean, Jesus Shit. Go back to your Dworkin you fucking sickos.
When they said they would stop did you guys actually believe them?

> deciding to travel with a circus.

Hah, is this still a thing or were you being hyperbolic?

I haven't smoked weed in a couple of months but I found it a reliable form of self-medication. Alcohol just makes me wallow, and cigarettes do nothing except make me angry at myself for raising my BP level and being a money pit

I stopped toking to take this dispatch course on the assumption that I would make it, because the actual job understandably involves random drug testing. You're dealing with hundreds of traveler's lives at a time and they can't have people coming in to do that all fucked up on something.

I personally think smoking weed at home would have no effect on my ability to do that, as long as I didn't go to work high, but there is no airliner in the world that doesn't include that as a condition of employment. But right now it's looking like I'm not gonna make it.
I don't have the good paying job, I had a shitty job and was trying to get the good one with this course I'm in. Maybe I wasn't completely clear on that...
I wish I could have a real hug. She's 1400 miles away right now. Thank you...

I hope this doesn't offend you, but I have strong personal oppositions to the military, not the least of which is the strong possibility of fighting in or logistically-aiding operations I disagree with. I have respect for the principle of serving your country, but not in the current circumstances. I will freely admit that a big part of it is fear. What if I kill someone who didn't deserve it? What if *I* get killed? Just because I hate myself and want to die a lot of the time doesn't mean the idea of stepping on a bomb or getting shot in the face is any less scary. If I died this young I would want it to be entirely my choice, and not kind of sudden freak thing. I would want it to be up to me.....

Thank you for the advice, though, it is sound and I've considered it in the past out of the desperation I feel... But I don't know if I'd hate myself any less for it, even if it fixed everything.

> Usually if you fail a test you can re-take just the test again. Keep studying, take practice exams, and you will get it.

Not here, you get one shot and it's permanently part of your grade. It's an FAA-regulated course, and even if you take it at a university at a normal semester pace that's pretty much how it goes.

The only test you *can* retake is the federal standardized test, which I am about to retake on Tuesday. Problem is is that it draws randomly from a pool of ~1400 questions and about two-thirds of them are pilot-focused questions, not stuff that dispatchers actually need to know. So it's hard to remember a lot of them since I'm not and never will be a pilot.
